tagging_basis: OCR H432 numbered specification sections (lettered learning outcomes as evidence)

units.label: 1(a)
units.summary: Explain why CF4 has polar bonds but no overall dipole.

units.label: 1(b)
units.summary: Explain why some water molecules have a relative molecular mass of 20.

units.label: 1(c)
units.summary: Calculate the partial pressure of oxygen from its percentage by volume and total pressure.

units.label: 1(d)
units.summary: Calculate the mass of carbon dioxide formed from combusting a volume of propane at RTP.
units.difficulty_basis: Two steps with unit conversion from m3

units.label: 1(e)
units.summary: Find the new initial rate when pH changes for a reaction first order in H+.
units.difficulty_basis: Link pH to concentration and order

units.label: 1(f)
units.summary: Calculate the number of oxygen atoms in a given mass of P2O5.
units.difficulty_basis: Mole and Avogadro calculation with ratio

units.label: 2(a)
units.summary: Write an ionic equation for carbonate ions forming an alkaline solution in water.

units.label: 2(b)
units.summary: Explain why acidifying the mixture is needed to obtain benzoic acid crystals.
units.difficulty_basis: Needs idea of protonating the carboxylate salt

units.label: 2(c)
units.summary: Write the overall equation for oxidation of phenylmethanol to benzoic acid using [O].

units.label: 2(d)
units.summary: Calculate the percentage yield of benzoic acid using density and volume.

units.label: 2(e)
units.summary: Describe how to recrystallise impure benzoic acid crystals.

units.label: 3(a)(i)
units.summary: Write the equation for reduction of Pb3O4 by methane.

units.label: 3(a)(ii)
units.summary: State one further safety precaution with a reason for heating lead oxide in methane.

units.label: 3(a)(iii)
units.summary: Suggest two modifications to ensure all oxygen is removed from lead oxide, with reasons.

units.label: 3(a)(iv)
units.summary: Calculate the empirical formula of a lead oxide from mass data.

units.label: 3(b)
units.summary: Identify lattice types in SiO2 and CO2 and explain the difference in melting points.

units.label: 4(a)(i)
units.summary: Give the systematic name of chloroxylenol.
units.difficulty_basis: Substituted phenol naming with several substituents

units.label: 4(a)(ii)
units.summary: Predict the number of peaks in the C-13 NMR spectrum of chloroxylenol.
units.difficulty_basis: Symmetry analysis of a substituted ring

units.label: 4(a)(iii)
units.summary: Name the acidic functional group and describe a test for it.
units.difficulty_basis: Recall of phenol and simple test

units.label: 4(a)(iv)
units.summary: Write the dissociation equation and calculate Ka of chloroxylenol from pH and percentage composition.
units.difficulty_basis: Multi-step weak acid calculation in an unfamiliar context

units.label: 4(b)(i)
units.summary: Mark the chiral centre in the structure of alpha-terpineol.

units.label: 4(b)(ii)
units.summary: Explain E/Z isomerism and why only one isomer of alpha-terpineol exists in a ring.
units.difficulty_basis: Four-mark reasoning in unfamiliar cyclic context

units.label: 4(b)(iii)
units.summary: Choose a reagent for each functional group in alpha-terpineol and draw the products.
units.difficulty_basis: Selective reactions on a multifunctional molecule

units.label: 5(a)(i)
units.summary: Calculate the enthalpy of solution from experimental data and use an energy cycle to find the enthalpy of reaction.
units.difficulty_basis: Six-mark data processing with cycle and signs

units.label: 5(a)(ii)
units.summary: Calculate the temperature change from a 20 percent uncertainty with a 0.1 C thermometer.

units.label: 5(b)
units.summary: Determine the standard entropy of anhydrous sodium thiosulfate using Gibbs and entropy data.
units.difficulty_basis: Four-step entropy and free energy calculation

units.label: 5(c)(i)
units.summary: Predict the bond angle and shape of the thiosulfate ion.
units.difficulty_basis: Shape prediction for an unfamiliar ion

units.label: 5(c)(ii)
units.summary: Draw a displayed formula for the tetrathionate ion.

units.label: 6(a)(i)
units.summary: Write the formulae of the iron hydroxide and silver sulfide precipitates.

units.label: 6(a)(ii)
units.summary: Explain whether the reaction of iron(II) sulfide with acid is a redox reaction.

units.label: 6(a)(iii)
units.summary: Write the equation for the reaction of hexaaquairon(II) with chlorine.

units.label: 6(a)(iv)
units.summary: Construct the equation for hydrogen sulfide reacting with acidified permanganate.
units.difficulty_basis: Half equation combination with unfamiliar sulfur product

units.label: 6(b)
units.summary: Deduce formulae of a hydrated iron compound, its decomposition products and gases from mass and volume data.
